verdict.rationale: cubic's AI wiki automatically indexes the whole codebase and produces searchable documentation with source links and architecture diagrams, so no manual context-file selection is needed. Its MCP server also exposes codebase context to coding agents. However, the interactive, agent-driven explanation the story describes is only documented for PR-scoped chat and code you select yourself, and the evidence never shows an agent walking a developer through an unfamiliar repository on demand. missing for 10: documented conversational agent explanation of an entire repo (not PR-scoped), detail on wiki depth and coverage of large codebases, independent or hands-on corroboration of wiki quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent map and explain an entire unfamiliar codebase without manually selecting context files

citations.quote: cubic's AI wiki automatically indexes your codebase and produces searchable wikis, complete with links to source code, architecture diagrams, and more.
cubic exports the wiki as markdown files into a directory in your repo (default `.cubic/wiki`) and keeps them current through a rolling pull request.
Connect cubic's MCP server to your coding agent to read review findings and codebase context
